## Introduction

In previous posts I have described how to use the self-contained Python scripts feature in the *uv* package manager to create [uv virtual environments for the nbstata Jupyter kernel](https://remlapmot.github.io/post/2025/nbstata-uv-venv/) to run Quarto documents with Stata code and to run Quarto documents using the [`jupyter: python3` engine](https://remlapmot.github.io/post/2025/self-contained-python-script-for-quarto/). In this post I describe how to do the same for Quarto documents using the knitr engine (i.e., running R code).

I recently discovered that there are now 3 *uv* inspired package managers for R; *ir*, *uvr*, and *rv* (maybe there are more?). I will concentrate on the first two as they allow defining self-contained R scripts.

## Automation with `just` in a complex directory structure

```makefile
render dir=invocation_directory():
    cd "{{ dir }}" && Rscript render.R
ir dir=invocation_directory():
    cd "{{ dir }}" && ir run render.R
uvr dir=invocation_directory():
    cd "{{ dir }}" && uvr run render.R
```

### Bonus 2 -- Making the render script executable

With both [`ir`]() and `uvr` (and indeed [`uv`]()) we can optionally make the _render.R_ script executable, say renaming to simply _render_ by adding the relevant shebang to the top of the file

```r
#!/usr/bin/env -S ir run
```

or

```r
#!/usr/bin/env -S uvr run
```

and making it executable

```sh
chmod +x render
```

then simply run with

```sh
./render
```

## Summary

I have shown how to make a self-contained, and optionally executable, R script to render Quarto documents using the knitr engine which automatically manage the required R packages. This functionality is provided by both the `ir` and `uvr` package managers. And this approach would also work for RMarkdown documents.
